title: Isolation of Nuclei from Murine Cardiac Tissue for Multiomic Sequencing
author: Veras, Eken, et al.
materials: CRITICAL: Keep the buffers on wet ice before adding to the tissue or nuclei.
The single-nucleus RNA-seq and single-nucleus ATAC-seq Fastq data processing have been conducted on a MacOS computer. 16 GB RAM should be sufficient for the initial analysis.

Prepare all fresh solutions on the day of the experiment and keep them on wet ice throughout the procedure to preserve nuclei integrity and minimize degradation.CRITICAL: Prepare fresh buffers before use and keep the buffers on wet ice before adding to the tissue/nuclei. All the tubes containing tissue and nuclei must be always on wet ice. Autoclave and treat all equipment with RNaseZap to reduce contamination. RNAse can greatly reduce nuclei yield and contribute to degradation artifacts within the cDNA. All surfaces and equipment should be decontaminated, and reagents must stay cold throughout the procedure to reduce the activity of RNAses/DNAses.1.Prepare the following solutions fresh on the day of the experiment and keep them on wet ice throughout the procedure: Homogenization buffer 01-04, Centrifuge buffer 01, Sorting buffer, 1x Lysis Buffer, Lysis Dilution Buffer, 0.1× Lysis Buffer, Wash Buffer, and Diluted Nuclei Buffer.2.Prepare the following items and place them on ice:a.A 50 mL gentleMACS C Tube containing 2.5 mL of Homogenization buffer 02.b.Two 15 mL Protein LoBind centrifuge tubes containing 2 mL Centrifuge buffer 01.c.Two empty 15 mL Protein LoBind centrifuge tubes.

steps.title: Select tissue amount
steps.instruction: Use one whole snap‑frozen murine left ventricle weighing approximately 20–40 mg; this amount is optimal for recovering ~15,000 nuclei per sample and for preparing final nuclei suspensions at 4,000–8,000 nuclei/µL for downstream 10x Genomics Chromium multi‑omic sequencing.

steps.title: Prepare fresh buffers
steps.instruction: On the day of the experiment prepare the following solutions fresh and keep them on wet ice at all times: Homogenization buffer 01‑04, Centrifuge buffer 01, Sorting buffer, 1× Lysis Buffer, Lysis Dilution Buffer, 0.1× Lysis Buffer, Wash Buffer, and Diluted Nuclei Buffer.

steps.title: Prepare equipment and tubes on ice
steps.instruction: Autoclave all equipment and treat surfaces and tubes with RNaseZap to eliminate RNase/DNase contamination. Keep all tubes on wet ice. Prepare: (a) a 50 mL gentleMACS C‑Tube containing 2.5 mL Homogenization buffer 02; (b) two 15 mL Protein LoBind centrifuge tubes each containing 2 mL Centrifuge buffer 01; (c) two empty 15 mL Protein LoBind centrifuge tubes.

steps.title: Enrich nuclei from tissue
steps.instruction: Homogenize the frozen cardiac tissue in the prepared homogenization buffer, filter the homogenate, and perform cushion centrifugation to enrich cardiac nuclei. Subsequently apply fluorescence‑activated nuclei sorting (FANS) to remove remaining debris and aggregates, yielding a clean nuclei suspension suitable for single‑nucleus multi‑omic sequencing.

steps.title: Single‑nuclei QC and library preparation
steps.instruction: Carry out quality control of the isolated nuclei and prepare snRNA‑seq and snATAC‑seq libraries (total timing ≈ 2 days). After library construction, you may pause the workflow and store the completed libraries at –20 °C for several months before sequencing.

steps.title: Set up computational environment
steps.instruction: Use a MacOS computer with at least 16 GB RAM. Install Cell Ranger ARC v2.0.2, R version 4.3.3, Seurat v5.2.0 and Signac v1.16.0 (required for downstream analysis of the Chromium Single Cell Multiome ATAC + Gene Expression data).

steps.title: Process sequencing data
steps.instruction: Run the Cell Ranger ARC pipeline (v2.0.2) against the mm10‑2020‑A reference to generate ATAC and gene‑expression matrices, then continue analysis with Seurat/Signac as described in the manuscript.
